docs.text: Dockup ¶ Docker Engine in a dedicated WSL distro, driven from Windows. No Docker Desktop, no services, no autostart unless you ask for it: one static dockup.exe imports a prebuilt Debian image into WSL as dockup , runs dockerd there under systemd, and bridges the Windows Docker CLI to it over a named pipe (plus an optional 127.0.0.1 TCP bridge). Why dockup? ¶ One distro, one job. A disposable Debian distro named dockup that exists only to run the Docker daemon. Your other distros are never touched. Native CLI feel. run -it , exec , logs -f , and Compose all behave natively over a raw byte-copy bridge, so you don't need -i workarounds, TCP ports, or firewall rules by default. Nothing runs unless you start it. Foreground ( dockup ) or background ( dockup daemon start ), plus opt-in startup at Windows login. Self-healing. doctor repairs stale state, --fix rebuilds a broken engine, and restore resets tampering while keeping your images. Quickstart ¶ dockup setup # install the dockup distro (asks where + which arch) dockup daemon start # run in the background dockup context use # make Docker use dockup by default docker run --rm hello-world dockup daemon stop # stop when done Prefer to leave your default Docker context alone? Use docker -H npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine ... or the per-command docker --context dockup ... . Or run in the foreground with dockup (Ctrl+C stops it). Commands ¶ Command What it does dockup Foreground run, logs inline, Ctrl+C stops dockup setup [--amd\|--arm] [--path=DIR] [--dry-run] Download, verify, and import the signed image (with a source fallback) dockup uninstall Remove the distro data (keeps the cached image and default path) dockup prune [--all] [--volumes] [--keep-image] Reclaim in-distro space and delete the cached image dockup restore [--full] Reset tampering (light) or reinstall from scratch ( --full ) dockup ps STATUS ( running / starting... / stopped ) + AUTOSTART table dockup context [use\|off] Show, activate, or deactivate the dockup Docker CLI context dockup daemon start\|stop\|restart\|status\|log Background process management + log follow dockup daemon autostart [on\|off] Show or set starting at Windows login (default off) dockup shutdown Stop everything and terminate the distro dockup doctor [--fix] Health checks; --fix reinstalls/repairs a broken engine dockup upgrade (alias update ) Update the in-distro engine to the latest versions; refresh the cached image dockup version Show the version dockup help [command] Help ( -h / --help work on every command) Where to go next ¶ Using dockup? Start with Installation , then Getting Started . Hacking on dockup? Read Architecture , then Building & Testing . Want to help? See Contributing .

docs.text: Contributing ¶ Issues and pull requests are welcome at CHE3MZ/dockup . Please use the bug/feature templates and the pull request checklist; they encode the rules below. Testing. Most testing runs in the cloud through this project's GitHub Actions workflows, though a local run is fine when you can do one. Test your changes, and don't open a PR for untested or unreviewed work. Push only after the build and the linters are clean; that keeps the code easy to maintain and review. Short commit messages. Keep them short and readable. Skip "updated something" and "fixed something"; a one-line summary of what the commit adds or removes is enough. Bug checks. Run the linters and other checkers as you change things. scripts\ops\go-bugcheck.sh and scripts\ops\go-seccheck.sh write their output to the logs folder. Install whatever they need first. Running these linters is a must for big changes. Tests. Run and add tests when possible or needed. Docs. Document your changes in docs/docs when possible. Comments. Add comments next to your changes when possible. Frozen strings. CI greps them, so never reword: the setup banner flow, dockup has not been setup yet run "dockup setup" to set it up. , starting... , test results : , autostart: on/off , STATUS/AUTOSTART/INSTALLED/SIZE/MEMORY , read-only , ok: autostart on , dry run complete . Green before review. Most workflows run automatically, so check that they all pass before you submit. If one is red, find out why.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ One static Windows binary, one disposable distro, one raw byte stream. Windows side (dockup.exe, Go, single static binary) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── docker.exe (user-installed, NOT bundled) │ npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine (HTTP-over-pipe, hijack-capable) ▼ dockup foreground (`dockup`) OR dockup daemon child (`dockup __serve`) │ go-winio ListenPipe, per-connection goroutine ▼ wsl -d dockup -u root -- socat STDIO UNIX-CONNECT:/var/run/docker.sock WSL side (distro "dockup", Debian 12, systemd=true) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── systemd (PID 1) → containerd.service → docker.service │ unix:///var/run/docker.sock ▼ socat bridge (one per client conn, spawned by Windows side) containers Design decisions ¶ Raw byte-copy, no HTTP parsing. Hijacked streams ( run -it , exec , logs -f , TTY resize) only survive a transparent proxy; anything that parses HTTP breaks them. No TCP hop. WSL2 NAT loopback can't reliably reach a distro-bound 127.0.0.1 , so the bridge speaks to the engine over socat STDIO per connection instead. TCP exists only as an opt-in 127.0.0.1 listener on the Windows side. Message-mode pipe. The listener uses MessageMode: true so a client's stdin close arrives server-side as EOF; the bridge then half-closes socat stdin and gives the container a 60s grace period to flush and exit. Loud failures. If the backend dies before producing a byte, the client gets HTTP 500 instead of a silent empty reply, and the daemon log records why. dockup_engine , not docker_engine . CI runners and user machines already hold Docker Desktop's pipe, so hijacking it would fake a pass. Debian rootfs, not nocloud. The cloud disk.raw tarballs fail wsl --import ; the debuerreotype rootfs tarballs (same bookworm content) import cleanly. Prebuilt image. scripts/image/ builds bookworm with the engine already installed, /etc/wsl.conf set, and units enabled, then signs the checksum with an ed25519 key. CI smoke-tests the import on windows-latest and publishes the assets to the release. internal/image downloads the signed checksum, verifies the signature against an embedded public key, verifies the tarball SHA256, caches it under <root>\cache\images , and imports from there; the from-source rootfs + apt flow remains an automatic fallback. Install root split. One user-chosen root holds distro\ (the wsl --import target) and cache\images\ (the verified image). Uninstall removes distro\ only, so the cache survives for reinstall; dockup prune is the only thing that deletes the cache. Legacy installs kept ext4.vhdx directly in the root, which the path helpers still detect. Single source of truth. installed lives only in %APPDATA%\dockup\state.json (locked read-modify-write); ~/.dockup/config.json holds user intent only. Old config files carrying the key still load; the key is ignored and dropped on next save. systemd reboot. One wsl --terminate dockup after writing wsl.conf so systemd becomes PID 1; every unit (re)start is preceded by systemctl reset-failed (start-limit throttling) and followed by a WaitDaemon poll (boot race). Install scripts end with apt-get clean because a dynamic VHDX only grows.

docs.text: Building & Testing ¶ Host rule (non-negotiable) ¶ The dev machine is compile/lint only . Never run dockup setup/run/daemon locally, never touch WSL, never download distro payloads, never install software on the host. All functional testing goes through GitHub Actions via the gh CLI, and every test run is preceded by git commit + git push . Allowed on host: go build ./... go vet ./... gofmt -l . go test ./... # unit only (part of bugcheck) sh scripts/ops/go-bugcheck.sh # busybox sh OK (skips the gopls step) sh scripts/ops/go-seccheck.sh Version stamping (as CI does it): go build -ldflags "-X github.com/CHE3MZ/dockup/internal/config.Version=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" -o dockup.exe ./cmd/dockup Unstamped builds fall back to the module version ( go install ) or the short commit SHA ( go build ); release builds are stamped with the v* tag by GoReleaser (see Releasing ). Or build both arches at once: .\scripts\build.ps1 # → dist/dockup-windows-amd64.exe + dist/dockup-windows-arm64.exe (stamped, gitignored) gh runbook ¶ git add -A; git commit -m "<short>"; git push gh run list --limit 7 gh run view <ID> --log # full text; never trust green/red blindly gh workflow run <name> [-f full-setup=true] git add -A sweeps parallel uncommitted edits into your commit. Always run git status / git diff first and report what rode along. CI map (all on push + dispatch; ci also on pull requests) ¶ Workflow Proves ci vet, go test -race , version-stamped build + smoke e2e-wsl WSL smoke: version/doctor/ps, refusal cases, foreign-pipe branch full-test (~7 min) End-to-end: setup → daemon → pipe/TCP/compose/stdin/TTY/exec/logs → upgrade → restore → uninstall scoop-test Real scoop-installed docker + docker-compose via DOCKER_HOST inspect-wsl Distro audit, provenance manifest, upgrade, break → doctor --fix , --full , reinstall reproducibility multi-distro Neighbor distros untouched; shutdown → starting... → self-heal; scoped uninstall arm-test arm64 vet/unit/build always; --arm install gated on a WSL probe (arm images currently lack WSL) release GoReleaser Windows binaries + checksums; publishes on v* tags (dispatch supports tag + dry_run ) image Prebuilt WSL rootfs: amd64+arm64 build, signed checksums, import + hello-world smoke; attaches to v* releases, rolling image-latest weekly PowerShell-in-CI pitfalls (learned the hard way) ¶ $LASTEXITCODE persists: steps tolerating nonzero native exits must end exit 0 . -match on arrays returns elements (truthy!): (cmd) -join " n"` first. wsl.exe emits raw UTF-16LE intermittently: strip NULs before matching; Go side already decodes. Single-element arrays, echo x | pipeline stdin closing, wsl -- <quoted args> mangling (quoteless one-liners; scripts via stdin in Go); follow existing patterns. Start-Job stdin piping is unreliable; prefer main-shell commands with timeouts. Frozen strings ¶ CI greps these verbatim, so never reword: the setup banner flow, dockup has not been setup yet run "dockup setup" to set it up. , starting... , test results : , autostart: on/off , STATUS/AUTOSTART/INSTALLED/SIZE/MEMORY , read-only , ok: autostart on , dry run complete . Exe icon ¶ cmd/dockup/winres/winres.json points at assets/icon.png ; the checked-in rsrc_windows_*.syso files are picked up automatically by go build . Regenerate after changing the art: cd cmd/dockup go run github.com/tc-hib/go-winres@latest make --arch amd64,arm64 Docs ¶ This site: docs/mkdocs.yml + docs/docs/ (theme vendored in docs/theme , so plain pip install mkdocs is enough). Build strictly before pushing: cd docs mkdocs build --strict

docs.text: Prebuilt WSL Image ¶ Status: the build, sign, smoke, and publish pipeline is green, and the client side has landed. dockup setup downloads, verifies, caches, and imports this image by default, with the from-source flow as an automatic fallback. Why ¶ Installing Docker inside a fresh WSL distro at setup time is the slowest and most fragile part of dockup setup : it depends on apt mirrors, DNS, and proxies working on the user's machine. A prebuilt rootfs turns that into a download and wsl --import . What's inside ¶ Debian 12 ( bookworm ) minbase docker-ce , docker-ce-cli , containerd.io , docker-buildx-plugin , docker-compose-plugin , socat ca-certificates , curl , gnupg , procps , iproute2 , systemd , systemd-sysv /etc/wsl.conf with [boot] systemd=true containerd.service , docker.service , and docker.socket enabled /etc/dockup-image with the build id, arch, suite, and engine versions Scrubbed before packing: machine-id (emptied so systemd regenerates it), /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf (WSL regenerates them), Docker and containerd state, apt lists/cache, logs, shell history, SSH host keys, random-seed , and the cross-build QEMU binary. Building ¶ Linux or WSL2, as root: sudo ./scripts/image/build.sh amd64 build sudo ./scripts/image/build.sh arm64 build Outputs: build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 Cross-building arm64 on an amd64 host installs qemu-user-static and uses binfmt, so the build takes noticeably longer. The tarball normalizes timestamps to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (0 by default) and uses gzip -n , and keeps numeric owners plus extended attributes. Package versions still float with the Debian and Docker repos, so two builds are reproducible only for the same package set. Signing ¶ go run ./scripts/image/imgtool keygen Store the printed seed= as the DOCKUP_IMAGE_SIGNING_KEY repository secret and keep the pub= value for the client to embed. The current public key lives in scripts/image/pubkey.txt . CI signs the checksum file: dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 -> dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sig Verify locally: go run ./scripts/image/imgtool verify \ -pub "$PUB" \ -in build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 \ -sig build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sig The signature is ed25519 over the exact bytes of the .sha256 file, written as base64. Verify the signature first, then the tarball against the checksum. Client ¶ internal/image owns the download, verification, and cache. dockup setup calls image.Ensure , which: resolves the release tag ( DOCKUP_IMAGE_TAG , else the binary's v* version, else image-latest ) and asset URLs; fetches <asset>.sha256 and <asset>.sig , verifies the signature against the embedded public key in internal/image/pubkey.go , and parses the SHA256; if a valid cache entry exists (signature, checksum, tarball, and metadata all match the current tag and arch), reuses it with no download; otherwise downloads the tarball to a .part file, verifies the SHA256, then atomically moves tarball, checksum, and signature into <install root>\cache\images and writes image-<arch>.json last. restore --full and setup re-import from the cache; dockup upgrade refreshes it (fetches the remote checksum/signature, downloads only if the release changed); dockup uninstall keeps it; dockup prune deletes it. The cache must verify before reuse, so a corrupted file is re-fetched rather than imported. Base URLs can be overridden for tests, mirrors, or air-gapped setups with DOCKUP_IMAGE_BASE_URL (default https://github.com/CHE3MZ/dockup/releases/download ) and DOCKUP_IMAGE_TAG . Verification against the embedded key is not optional. CI ¶ .github/workflows/image.yml builds both arches on every Monday at 04:00 UTC, on manual dispatch, and on every v* tag: build : rootfs, checksum, signature, artifacts smoke : imports the amd64 tarball on windows-latest , checks that systemd is PID 1, waits for dockerd, runs hello-world , then unregisters publish : checks each tarball against its .sha256 and verifies both signatures with scripts/image/pubkey.txt . On a v* tag it waits for the release created by release.yml and attaches the image assets to it; otherwise it replaces the assets on the image-latest rolling release Dispatch inputs: publish (default true) and tag (empty = rolling image-latest ; set it to attach to an existing versioned release). Versioned releases carry the Windows binaries from GoReleaser plus the image assets, and are the immutable reference. image-latest is explicitly not marked latest, so normal release links keep pointing at the versioned release. The arm64 artifact is built but not imported in CI: the Windows ARM runners do not ship wsl.exe yet (see arm-test.yml ). Rollout ¶ Build, sign, and smoke the image in CI (done). Teach dockup setup to download, verify, and import it, with the current from-source flow as an automatic fallback (done - internal/image plus the distro\ and cache\images\ layout). Setup no longer runs apt on the happy path; the install/configure scripts stay because the fallback, doctor , restore , and upgrade still use them. Security ¶ Verify the signature before importing; never after. Rotate the signing seed only together with scripts/image/pubkey.txt ; publish fails if a signature does not verify with the committed key. Keep the build script and workflow public so the artifact is reproducible. Rebuild on a schedule, otherwise the baked engine goes stale. Keep the from-source path as the escape hatch if an image is broken or a user does not want to trust the CI-built blob. The fallback path is weaker: it downloads debuerreotype's rootfs over HTTPS without a signature (the Docker packages installed afterwards come from Docker's GPG-signed apt repo). Prefer the signed image.

docs.text: go run ./scripts/image/imgtool keygen Store the printed seed= as the DOCKUP_IMAGE_SIGNING_KEY repository secret and keep the pub= value for the client to embed. The current public key lives in scripts/image/pubkey.txt . CI signs the checksum file: dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 -> dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sig Verify locally: go run ./scripts/image/imgtool verify \ -pub "$PUB" \ -in build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 \ -sig build/dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sig The signature is ed25519 over the exact bytes of the .sha256 file, written as base64. Verify the signature first, then the tarball against the checksum.
docs.title: Signing

docs.text: internal/image owns the download, verification, and cache. dockup setup calls image.Ensure , which: resolves the release tag ( DOCKUP_IMAGE_TAG , else the binary's v* version, else image-latest ) and asset URLs; fetches <asset>.sha256 and <asset>.sig , verifies the signature against the embedded public key in internal/image/pubkey.go , and parses the SHA256; if a valid cache entry exists (signature, checksum, tarball, and metadata all match the current tag and arch), reuses it with no download; otherwise downloads the tarball to a .part file, verifies the SHA256, then atomically moves tarball, checksum, and signature into <install root>\cache\images and writes image-<arch>.json last. restore --full and setup re-import from the cache; dockup upgrade refreshes it (fetches the remote checksum/signature, downloads only if the release changed); dockup uninstall keeps it; dockup prune deletes it. The cache must verify before reuse, so a corrupted file is re-fetched rather than imported. Base URLs can be overridden for tests, mirrors, or air-gapped setups with DOCKUP_IMAGE_BASE_URL (default https://github.com/CHE3MZ/dockup/releases/download ) and DOCKUP_IMAGE_TAG . Verification against the embedded key is not optional.
docs.title: Client

docs.text: .github/workflows/image.yml builds both arches on every Monday at 04:00 UTC, on manual dispatch, and on every v* tag: build : rootfs, checksum, signature, artifacts smoke : imports the amd64 tarball on windows-latest , checks that systemd is PID 1, waits for dockerd, runs hello-world , then unregisters publish : checks each tarball against its .sha256 and verifies both signatures with scripts/image/pubkey.txt . On a v* tag it waits for the release created by release.yml and attaches the image assets to it; otherwise it replaces the assets on the image-latest rolling release Dispatch inputs: publish (default true) and tag (empty = rolling image-latest ; set it to attach to an existing versioned release). Versioned releases carry the Windows binaries from GoReleaser plus the image assets, and are the immutable reference. image-latest is explicitly not marked latest, so normal release links keep pointing at the versioned release. The arm64 artifact is built but not imported in CI: the Windows ARM runners do not ship wsl.exe yet (see arm-test.yml ).
docs.title: CI

docs.text: Build, sign, and smoke the image in CI (done). Teach dockup setup to download, verify, and import it, with the current from-source flow as an automatic fallback (done - internal/image plus the distro\ and cache\images\ layout). Setup no longer runs apt on the happy path; the install/configure scripts stay because the fallback, doctor , restore , and upgrade still use them.
docs.title: Rollout

docs.text: Verify the signature before importing; never after. Rotate the signing seed only together with scripts/image/pubkey.txt ; publish fails if a signature does not verify with the committed key. Keep the build script and workflow public so the artifact is reproducible. Rebuild on a schedule, otherwise the baked engine goes stale. Keep the from-source path as the escape hatch if an image is broken or a user does not want to trust the CI-built blob. The fallback path is weaker: it downloads debuerreotype's rootfs over HTTPS without a signature (the Docker packages installed afterwards come from Docker's GPG-signed apt repo). Prefer the signed image.

docs.text: Releasing ¶ Releases use v* tags. A tag starts two workflows: release.yml : GoReleaser builds the Windows binaries and creates the GitHub release with GITHUB_TOKEN . image.yml : builds, signs, and smoke-tests both rootfs tarballs, then attaches them to the same release. The release is only usable once both finish. The image job fails if the release does not exist, so it cannot silently publish an image-only release. Assets ¶ Asset What it is dockup-windows-amd64.exe Windows amd64 binary, stamped with the tag dockup-windows-arm64.exe Windows arm64 binary, stamped with the tag dockup_checksums.txt SHA-256 for both binaries dockup-amd64.tar.gz Prebuilt WSL rootfs, amd64 dockup-arm64.tar.gz Prebuilt WSL rootfs, arm64 *.tar.gz.sha256 SHA-256 of the tarball *.tar.gz.sig ed25519 signature over the .sha256 bytes The rolling image-latest release still exists for weekly rebuilds; versioned releases are the immutable reference. Release notes ¶ Notes come from cliff.toml via git-cliff. release.yml renders the commits in the tag's range, then hands the file to GoReleaser with --release-notes . The prebuilt-image footer is added by the release section of .goreleaser.yaml . Preview them locally: task cliff # unreleased commits task release-notes # latest tag, writes RELEASE_NOTES.md Cutting a release ¶ From a clean main with all workflows green: git tag -a v1.1.0 -m "dockup v1.1.0" git push origin v1.1.0 Watch both runs and inspect the completed release: gh run list --workflow release.yml --limit 1 gh run list --workflow image.yml --limit 1 gh release view v1.1.0 If a run fails, fix it on main , delete the tag, and retag the fixed commit; do not move a tag after assets have been published. Manual dispatch ¶ Both workflows can be started without pushing a tag. # Build binaries without publishing; uploads dist/ as a workflow artifact. gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v1.1.0 -f dry_run=true # Build and publish images for an existing tag release. gh workflow run image.yml -f tag=v1.1.0 -f publish=true # Refresh the rolling release instead. gh workflow run image.yml -f publish=true release.yml requires the tag to exist and checks it out. image.yml with an empty tag input publishes to image-latest . Verifying a release ¶ sha256sum -c dockup_checksums.txt gh release download v1.1.0 -p 'dockup-amd64.tar.gz*' go run ./scripts/image/imgtool verify \ -pub "$(cat scripts/image/pubkey.txt)" \ -in dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 \ -sig dockup-amd64.tar.gz.sig dockup version prints the tag in release builds and go install builds. Local go build builds print the short commit SHA (with -dirty when the tree has uncommitted changes).

docs.text: Configuration ¶ First run creates ~/.dockup/config.json : { "default_path": "C:/WSL", "current_path": "C:/WSL", "port": 2375, "use_tcp": false, "pipe_name": "\\\\.\\pipe\\dockup_engine", "color": true, "autostart": false } Key Meaning default_path Prefilled install root for the next setup (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\dockup ); rewritten to whatever path you used on every successful setup current_path Install root of the live distro; holds distro\ and cache\images (cleared on uninstall) port / use_tcp Optional TCP bridge (default off). When on, it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, never on the LAN pipe_name Named pipe to serve (default \\.\pipe\dockup_engine ) color Master switch for CLI colors (also auto-off when piped, NO_COLOR , TERM=dumb , or CI) autostart Start at Windows login (managed via dockup daemon autostart on\|off ) docker_context_prev Context to restore on dockup context off (written by dockup context use ; safe to remove) Note Whether dockup is installed lives in %APPDATA%\dockup\state.json ( installed , plus arch , setupAt , daemon PID, and a package snapshot): the single source of truth. config.json holds only your intent, so it is safe to delete. Any dockup command recreates it with defaults. Warning The TCP bridge has no authentication. While it is on, any local process that can reach 127.0.0.1 can control the daemon, which is equivalent to root inside the distro. Leave it off unless you need it, and never forward the port through a firewall or proxy. Warning state.json is machine-managed (locked read-modify-write). Don't hand-edit it. dockup doctor repairs it if it ever goes stale.

docs.text: Getting Started ¶ Foreground or daemon? ¶ Mode Command Stops with Foreground dockup Ctrl+C Background dockup daemon start dockup daemon stop Only one may run at a time; the second starter refuses with a one-line message telling you what is already holding the bridge. Your first containers ¶ Setup creates a Docker CLI context named dockup that points at the bridge. Activate it once and every Docker client uses dockup: dockup context use docker version docker run --rm hello-world dockup context off switches Docker back to the context that was active before. Prefer to leave your default alone? Pick the context per command, or point at the pipe: docker --context dockup run --rm hello-world docker -H npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine run --rm hello-world The sticky environment-variable way (current shell only; it overrides any context): $env:DOCKER_HOST = 'npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine' docker run --rm hello-world docker run -it --rm debian:bookworm bash Interactive sessions, exec , and logs -f all work natively; see Using Docker . Checking status ¶ dockup ps STATUS AUTOSTART INSTALLED SIZE MEMORY running off yes 452 MB 128 MB STATUS is running (engine answering), starting... (bridge up, engine still booting), or stopped . AUTOSTART is on / off (Windows login autostart). INSTALLED is yes / no , SIZE is distro disk use, MEMORY its live RAM use. dockup ps --json prints the same row machine-readable for scripts. Stopping ¶ dockup daemon stop # stop the background bridge (distro stays warm for fast restart) dockup shutdown # stop everything, foreground included, and terminate the distro (ps => stopped) Ctrl+C in a foreground stops the bridge the same way daemon stop does. The distro itself stays warm in both cases; shutdown is the only thing that stops it. Ctrl+C not working at all? Run dockup shutdown from another terminal. It stops the stuck foreground too. Starting at Windows login (opt-in) ¶ dockup daemon autostart on # create the Startup entry (default off) dockup daemon autostart # query: autostart: on|off dockup daemon autostart off # remove the Startup entry

docs.text: Installation ¶ Requirements ¶ Windows 10/11 with WSL2 ( wsl --install ) A Windows Docker CLI, e.g. scoop install docker docker-compose dockup.exe on your PATH (Windows amd64 or arm64) Getting dockup.exe ¶ From a release ¶ Download dockup-windows-amd64.exe or dockup-windows-arm64.exe from the latest release , verify it against dockup_checksums.txt , rename it to dockup.exe , and put it on your PATH . From source ¶ Build from source (Go 1.24+): git clone https://github.com/CHE3MZ/dockup.git cd dockup go build -o dockup.exe ./cmd/dockup Running setup ¶ dockup setup Setup asks where to install dockup (any absolute path, e.g. D:/WSL/Dockup ; empty input keeps the shown default, which is whatever you used last, and --path skips the question), then confirms before touching anything: Setting up dockup: dockup will install and configure a new instance on WSL under the name "dockup" proceed? [y/n] It then downloads the signed prebuilt image for your architecture from the matching GitHub release (plain HTTPS, no GitHub account or token), verifies its ed25519 signature and SHA256 checksum, caches it in <install root>\cache\images , and imports it into <install root>\distro . The image already contains Debian, Docker, systemd, and the enabled engine units, so setup only has to configure and start them. Each stage ends with test results : success . If the image cannot be fetched or verified, setup warns and falls back to the older source path: download the official Debian rootfs and install Docker from Docker's apt repo inside the distro. That fallback rootfs is fetched over HTTPS only, not signature-checked; prefer the signed image and treat the fallback as an escape hatch. If a stage fails you get something went wrong, retry or abort? [retry/abort] . The install root defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%\dockup . The cached image is about 200 MB per architecture and is reused by reinstalls, restore --full , and dockup upgrade ; dockup prune deletes it when you want the space back. Finishing prints: you're all good to go! run "dockup" to start a foreground process or "dockup daemon start" to start a background daemon process. Useful flags ¶ Flag Effect --amd / --arm Distro architecture (default --amd ) --path=DIR Install root (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\dockup ; becomes the new default on success) --dry-run Print distro name, install root, image/cache paths, URLs + sizes, pipe/TCP plan - changes nothing Folder layout ¶ <install root>\ distro\ # wsl --import target (ext4.vhdx, disk, etc.) cache\images\ # verified setup image: .tar.gz, .sha256, .sig, image-<arch>.json Uninstall removes distro\ and keeps cache\images\ , so a later setup does not download the image again. dockup prune removes the cache. Installs created by older dockup versions kept ext4.vhdx directly in the install root; setup and uninstall still recognize that layout, and the next install uses distro\ . Reinstalling ¶ If a dockup distro already exists, setup asks: Warning: an installation of dockup already exists on WSL. Delete it and let dockup reinstall? [y/n] Answering n aborts cleanly with exit code 0 and changes nothing. Answering y re-imports from the cached image when it still matches the running binary's release, so reinstalling is normally fast and offline-friendly. Verify it works ¶ dockup daemon start docker -H npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine run --rm hello-world

docs.text: Maintenance ¶ Daemon lifecycle ¶ dockup daemon start # refuses if already running (foreground or daemon) dockup daemon stop dockup daemon restart dockup daemon status # running (daemon pid ..., pipe ok) / stopped; exit code matches dockup daemon log # follow the log, read-only, Ctrl+C to exit Full shutdown and uninstall ¶ dockup shutdown # stop everything (daemon + any foreground) + terminate the distro dockup uninstall # confirm [y/n], unregister the distro, clear state Uninstall deletes the distro data under <root>\distro only. It keeps the install root, the cached setup image under <root>\cache\images , and default_path , so the next setup re-imports without downloading. It removes the Startup entry and is idempotent - running it twice still exits 0. --force skips the confirmation (same for restore ). Reclaiming disk space ¶ The distro disk only ever grows. Reclaim Docker objects without reinstalling: dockup prune # in-distro Docker prune + delete the cached image dockup prune --all # plus all unused images dockup prune --volumes # plus unused volumes (destroys their data) dockup prune --keep-image # Docker prune only, keep the cached image prune deletes the cached setup image by default and works even after uninstall , when only the cache is left. Every form confirms first ( --force skips it). Health and repair ¶ dockup doctor # checks WSL, distro, systemd, socket, pipe, config; repairs stale PIDs/paths dockup doctor --fix # also reinstalls + reconfigures a broken in-distro engine dockup upgrade # confirm [y/n], update the engine to latest, restart services, verify dockup update # alias for upgrade upgrade also refreshes the cached setup image when one exists: it fetches the current checksum and signature and only re-downloads the tarball if the release changed. A refresh failure is a warning, not a failed upgrade. doctor --fix is engine-only repair. For tampering around the engine (extra packages, broken configs), use restore : dockup restore # confirm [y/n]: remove packages added since setup, # reinstall engine set, rewrite managed configs, # restart services. Images, containers, volumes survive. dockup restore --full # confirm [y/n]: delete + reinstall the whole distro. # Guaranteed pristine; containers, images, volumes are destroyed. # Re-imports the cached image; accepts --amd/--arm/--path overrides. Rule of thumb: doctor --fix when the engine won't answer, restore when the distro was fiddled with, restore --full when you want factory-fresh.

docs.text: dockup shutdown # stop everything (daemon + any foreground) + terminate the distro dockup uninstall # confirm [y/n], unregister the distro, clear state Uninstall deletes the distro data under <root>\distro only. It keeps the install root, the cached setup image under <root>\cache\images , and default_path , so the next setup re-imports without downloading. It removes the Startup entry and is idempotent - running it twice still exits 0. --force skips the confirmation (same for restore ).

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptom Meaning / fix dockup has not been setup yet run "dockup setup" to set it up. Nothing installed. Run dockup setup distro "dockup" is missing from WSL Removed outside dockup (e.g. wsl --unregister ). State was cleared automatically. Run dockup doctor , then dockup setup distro "dockup" is present but not responding Distro broken. Run dockup doctor --fix to repair it pipe is held by another program / pipe held by another program, not dockup Something else holds dockup_engine (a second dockup foreground/daemon, or Docker Desktop, which owns docker_engine ). Stop it first Bare docker talks to the wrong daemon Docker Desktop holds the default pipe. Stop it, or point at dockup explicitly with -H npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine ps shows starting... Bridge is up, engine still booting. Wait; it flips to running via systemd self-heal dockup is not installed — autostart skipped Login boot with nothing installed. Run dockup setup first stopped (stale daemon pid ... — run dockup doctor) Crash or reboot leftover. dockup doctor clears it Ctrl+C doesn't stop the foreground Press it again; the second interrupt forces exit. Or run dockup shutdown from another terminal Corrupt config.json Tolerated (warns, continues with defaults); delete it and any command recreates it wsl --version fails Update WSL ( wsl --update ); systemd needs a recent Store WSL prebuilt image unavailable warning Setup could not download or verify the image and fell back to the source install. Usually a transient network or GitHub issue Setup download stalls Needs internet; the image lands under <root>\cache\images ( .part while in flight, removed by dockup prune ) and source fallback uses %TEMP%\dockup-rootfs-*.tar.gz Image checksum/signature mismatch Tampered or truncated download. Run dockup prune to drop the cache, then dockup setup again Setup import fails from a cached image dockup prune discards the cache and retries source. Report the release if it keeps failing If the engine answers inside WSL ( wsl -d dockup -u root -- docker version ) but not through the pipe, check dockup daemon log and dockup doctor . If the distro itself was modified, run dockup restore before anything drastic. For hands-on debugging, open a shell right inside the distro, with no wsl.exe flags to remember: dockup ssh # interactive shell dockup ssh -- journalctl -u docker.service -n 30 # one remote command

docs.text: Using Docker ¶ Any Docker client that speaks npipe:// works: the docker.exe from docker.com , scoop install docker , VS Code's Docker extension (set its host), and Compose. No flags needed on most machines: while dockup runs, it also serves the default docker_engine pipe, so plain docker ps just works. (If Docker Desktop is running and holds that name, keep using -H / DOCKER_HOST below.) Docker contexts ¶ Setup creates a Docker CLI context named dockup that points at the bridge. This is the cleanest way to select it, and it composes with Compose and IDE Docker integrations: dockup context use # make dockup Docker's current context docker ps dockup context off # restore the context used before dockup context on its own shows the context's host and which context is active. For a single command, skip activation: docker --context dockup ps An active context only applies when DOCKER_HOST is unset: the environment variable always wins. Uninstall removes the dockup context when it still points at the configured pipe. Connection strings ¶ Bridge Address Named pipe (always on) npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine TCP (opt-in, see Configuration ) tcp://127.0.0.1:2375 (or your custom port) Note The pipe is dockup_engine , not docker_engine ; that name belongs to Docker Desktop, and dockup deliberately avoids hijacking it. Everyday commands ¶ $env:DOCKER_HOST = 'npipe:////./pipe/dockup_engine' docker run --rm hello-world docker run -it --rm debian:bookworm bash docker exec -it <container> sh docker logs -f <container> Compose ¶ With the Compose plugin: docker compose up --abort-on-container-exit docker compose build docker compose down The classic docker-compose binary works too. Just export DOCKER_HOST first so it finds the bridge. Builds work as well: the client streams the build context to the daemon over the same pipe. Bind mounts ¶ The daemon runs on Linux inside the distro, so a Windows host path does not exist for it: docker run -v C:\proj:/app ... # fails: no such path in the distro docker run -v ./data:/data ... # Compose resolves this to a Windows path too Use named volumes instead; they live in the distro and work everywhere: services: app: image: alpine volumes: - data:/var/lib/app volumes: data: If you need to edit bind-mounted files from Windows, keep the project inside the distro instead and open it through \\wsl$\dockup\... . What "native" means here ¶ The bridge is a raw byte-copy per connection straight into the in-distro engine socket, so HTTP-hijacked streams ( run -it , exec , logs -f , attach ) behave exactly like a local daemon. There is no protocol parsing in the middle to break them, including terminal resize, which is just another API call multiplexed over the same stream.
